headline: A 2016 law lets federal law enforcement officers keep carrying their government-issued firearms during planned furloughs, such as budget-related work stoppages.
what_it_does: The law allows a federal law enforcement officer to carry a government-issued firearm during a covered furlough. A covered furlough is a planned event in which an agency involuntarily furloughs employees because of downsizing, reduced funding, lack of work, or budget limits, including a lapse in appropriations. The summary describes only this section, so other parts of the law may not be covered here.

who_it_affects.how: Officers who are furloughed may carry their government-issued firearms during a covered furlough.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that employ law enforcement officers
who_it_affects.how: Agencies that furlough law enforcement employees during a covered furlough are subject to this authorization for those officers.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 22, 2016; the available summary does not state a separate effective date.
